unit.why: A short first-person memorate, quoted from Megillat Setarim, about the author's ruah ha-kodesh between the ages of two and five and his uncle R. Zvi of Zhidachov paying him weekly to tell what he saw.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a numbered series of praises; the next division (ח) continues the same theme (R. Zvi blessing him to stop saying ruah ha-kodesh at age six) but is a separate anecdote.

stories.start_quote: במגלת סתרים כתי״ק וזה"ל מיום שהייתי
stories.summary_en: From age two to five the author (R. Yitzhak Eizik of Komarno) had wondrous visions, prophetic speech and sight from one end of the world to the other; his uncle and teacher R. Zvi of Zhidachov paid him two coins a week to tell and answer his questions, and the child gave the money to charity.

quotes: צפיתי מסוף העולם עד סופו ממש
והשגת רוח הקודש ודברתי דברי נביאות
tags.why: The child has ruah ha-kodesh and sees across the world.

quotes: ודברתי דברי נביאות כאשר נשאל איש בדבר אלקים
tags.why: Prophetic disclosure, likened to inquiring of God.
He gave the coins to charity.

quotes: ומורי דודי איש אלקים נורא וקדוש
נתן לי שני ריינוש בכל שבוע
tags.why: His teacher and uncle questions and rewards him.

quotes: ומורי דודי איש אלקים נורא וקדוש
tags.why: His uncle appears; an uncle is not immediate family.
A praise of the tzaddik's holiness and gifts from early childhood.
The source is the author's private 'scroll of secrets' manuscript.
